blocks.x: There are generally two types of people when it comes to vacationing at sea: cruise people and non-cruise people. It’s rare to find an ambivalent traveler somewhere in between. I, for one, am firmly a cruise person, in part because I grew up around it—my parents both worked in the cruise industry, and we always lived near a port, meaning we were regularly going on cruises or welcoming guests over for dinner who had just disembarked one.

Over the years, between family vacations and work trips as a travel editor, I’ve been on dozens of ships and cruise lines. And while I haven't sailed on Celebrity Cruises yet, it’s high on my wish list. It has a reputation as a solid premium cruise line, sitting in a nice sweet spot between the massive family-friendly lines and the ultra-luxury smaller ship operators, with great food to boot, including restaurants with menus designed by chef Daniel Boulud. The Edge Class ships are particularly appealing, with Infinite Veranda staterooms that add open-air access to more cabins; the transformable moving Magic Carpet area; and a pool deck that more closely resembles a luxury resort than a traditional ship.

Celebrity sails to ports around the world, with popular itineraries heading to the Caribbean, Mediterranean, and Alaska. Cruises are rarely a small-ticket item, so whether you’ve got an itinerary on lock or are still perusing options, check back here before you book to make sure you’re not missing out on any promo codes or available discounts.
Sign up for emails and get a Celebrity Cruises discount code for up to $100 off your next vacation

Yes, promotional emails are already taking over our collective inboxes, but if you're willing to add another brand to the list, you could get up to $100 off your next cruise. Plus, you'll stay in the loop on other upcoming sales and new itineraries, so really, it's a win-win.
Get 75% off your second guest on Celebrity Cruises sailings in 2026

As part of its ongoing fall sale, Celebrity is offering 75% off your second guest’s cruise fare, plus savings of up to $700 per room (Celebrity river cruises and Galapagos expeditions are excluded); those going on an Alaska sailing can also score a $100 ‘Book now bonus.’

This is an easy way to bring down the cost of a trip for couples or friends traveling together, especially since it can be stacked with additional ways to save. It applies to select sailings of three nights or longer taken through May 10, 2028, and a promo code is not required. Itineraries range from weekend getaways—like a 3-Night Key West and Bahamas trip starting at $335 per person—to longer jaunts, like the 8-Night Aruba, Bonaire, & Curacao trip starting at $887 per person.

A few other notable itineraries included in the sale: the 7-Night Rhine River Christmas Cruise sailing over Christmas later this year; a 7-Night Dutch and Belgian Tulips river cruise on the new Celebrity Wanderer ship; and an 8-Night Aruba, Bonaire, and Curacao Caribbean cruise departing from Miami this November.
This fall, third, fourth, and fifth guests sail free
https://media.cntraveler.com/photos/68f90566c8b892b54c6e4f12/1:1/w_90%2Cc_limit/MF%2520hs.JPG

For bigger group trips, see if the sailing you’re interested in is one in which third, fourth, and fifth guests sail for free. This offer applies to new individual bookings made at standard rates on select sailings departing between now and May 10, 2028, excluding Celebrity river cruises, Galapagos sailings, and Alaska Cruisetours. It applies to Inside, Ocean View, Veranda, and Concierge Class staterooms only, and offers a $0 cruise fare for any additional guests in the same stateroom as the first full fare and second guest, so it’s best suited to families or friend groups comfortable sharing the same space. Of note, all other charges, including taxes, fees, and port expenses, do apply to all guests.
Save more on 2026 Celebrity sailings with last-minute cruise deals

Have some wiggle room in your calendar? You can snag discounted rates on last-minute cruises; 6–14 night sailings start at $459 per person, with itineraries around the globe—Japan, Alaska, the Norwegian fjords, the Caribbean, and the Mediterranean included. Shorter sailings, like a 4-Night Key West and Bahamas sailing, start at just $343 per person.
On the flip side, if you’re ready to lock in 2027 plans, you might be rewarded too: Book in advance for 2027 and find sailings from as little as $337 per person.
Sign up for Captain’s Club Rewards to access exclusive benefits & savings

Frequent Celebrity cruisers can gain access to exclusive benefits when they join the Captain’s Club. Like many rewards programs, this one offers a tiered benefits system. You gain access to tiers by reaching a points threshold, moving up from the Preview level to Classic, Select, Elite, Elite Plus, and finally Zenith. Points are earned based on stateroom category and number of nights sailed (i.e., for an Inside & Ocean View room, you’ll earn two Club points per night; for a splashy Iconic Suite, you’ll earn 24 points per night). Elite members need only reach 300 points; once there, they’ll gain access to free laundry services, Captain’s Club cocktail hour, and spa benefits. Reach 3,000 and you’ll achieve Zenith status, which gives you access to the Retreat Lounge as well as several complimentary services.
Save up to $100 per person with a Celebrity Cruises military discount

Celebrity Cruises offers exclusive military savings on select staterooms and sailings to Americans and Canadians who have served their country, including active duty service members, veterans, and retirees. Savings apply for the first and second guest based on your stateroom type, and can be combined with any of the line's other current promotions for even more savings. During the booking process, you'll be asked to verify your identity, and then the savings will automatically be applied: $25 per person for Inside or Ocean View staterooms, and $100 per person for Veranda, Concierge Class, AquaClass, or The Retreat staterooms.
What to do if your Celebrity Cruises promo code isn’t working

Having trouble getting a promo code to work correctly? There are a few ways to troubleshoot. Start by double-checking the basics—typos, extra spaces, or incorrect capitalization can all prevent a code from working as it should. You'll also want to confirm that the code is still valid, as expiration dates, minimum spend requirements, and itinerary exclusions may apply.
